[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]
== Biography ==
'''James Glasgow''' was baptised at Edinburgh on 16 March 1679, a son of [[Glasgow-2682|James Glasgow]] and [[Duffe-18|Elizabeth or Isobell Duffe]].<ref>“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950,” FamilySearch database, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC9-Q9N James Glasgow, 1679].</ref>

The same parents had another son named James, baptised on 18 April 1680.<ref>“Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950,” index entry for James Glasgow, baptised 18 April 1680 at Edinburgh, son of James Glasgow and Elizabeth/Isobell Duffe.</ref> These are consecutive child records, so [[Glasgow-3368|James Glasgow]] remains a distinct same-name sibling. Reuse of the name suggests that the elder child may have died before the later baptism, but no burial or other survival record proves that conclusion.

An Edinburgh banns-and-marriages index records James Glasgow and [[Dobie-449|Jean Dobie or Wood]] on 28 July 1698.<ref>Scotland's People, [https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/ Old Parish Registers], banns and marriages, Edinburgh parish 685/1, reference 450/47, 28 July 1698; index supplied 10 September 2026. The original entry has not been inspected.</ref> The index's “or Wood” is an alternative surname for Jean as indexed; it does not show whether it was an alias, prior surname or another convention.

This profile is attached to Jean, with sons [[Glasgow-3102|Peter Glasgow]] and [[Glasgow-2473|Robert Glasgow]], but those relationships remain uncertain. Peter's 1699 baptism proves an adult father James Glasgow at Edinburgh,<ref>“Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950,” FamilySearch database, [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:F3BL-B2K Peter Glasgow, 1699].</ref> not whether he was the child baptised in 1679 or his 1680 brother. No inspected record bridges either infant to the adult marriage or proves Robert's parentage.

== Research Notes ==
=== Current father-profile assessment, 20 October 2026 ===

The 1696 apothecary apprentice is a compatible later identity; the separate 1679 and 1680 baptisms and Dobie marriage question remain unresolved.

This 1679 child remains a compatible childhood comparison for the 1696 apothecary apprentice [[[Glasgow-4114|James Glasgow (Glasgow-4114)]]](/people/glasgow-4114.html), whose preferred father account is now [[[Glasgow-2682|James Glasgow (Glasgow-2682)]]](/people/glasgow-2682.html), probable 82%. The 1680 [same-name child](/people/glasgow-3368.html) remains separate and may be the survivor. Neither child is selected as that apprentice, and the 1698 Jean Dobie or Wood marriage does not identify a baptism. No spouse, mother, birth date or identity merger is changed.<ref>[https://www.tradeshouselibrary.org/uploads/4/7/7/2/47723681/edinburgh_apprentices_~_1666_to_1700_~_1929.pdf#page=47 Watson, Edinburgh Apprentices (1929), printed p.37, PDF p.47: James 1696 and Thomas 1699; printed page inspected 18 October, reused]; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC9-N9X Thomas, 13 November 1684: maintained FamilySearch baptism citation]; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC9-Q9J James, 16 March 1679: retained separate child comparison]; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQC9-8S4 James, 18 April 1680: retained separate child comparison]; [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FM3W-XBN Margaret, 20 March 1691: later daughter, not a younger son]. Prior inspected printed register and maintained baptism citations; no new original inspection.</ref>


Search Edinburgh burials from 16 March 1679 to 18 April 1680 and inspect the original 1698 marriage for residences, occupations, witnesses and Jean's stated name. Inspect Peter's original baptism to establish whether Jean Dobie is named as his mother. Treat this as a survival-and-adult-identity question, not a duplicate-profile question. Retain Jean Dobie or Wood, Peter and Robert as uncertain relationships pending that evidence.
